final_answer:
Upon CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition with AI-10-49 in inv(16) AML ME-1 cells, RUNX1 chromatin occupancy dramatically increases: the number of RUNX1 binding sites expands 6.9-fold (from 1,329 peaks in DMSO to 9,169 peaks in AI-10-49), and signal strength at pre-existing sites increases 2.7-fold on average (93.3% of shared sites gain signal). Importantly, 92.7% of baseline DMSO binding sites are retained, while 7,950 entirely new sites appear.

The newly gained RUNX1 binding sites are overwhelmingly (90%) located at active chromatin regions pre-marked by H3K27ac, indicating RUNX1 is released from CBFβ-SMMHC-mediated sequestration and recruited to enhancers and promoters. These sites include regulatory regions of key AML dependency genes: MYC gains RUNX1 binding at its upstream enhancer; CCND2 (cyclin D2) gains 5 RUNX1 peaks; CDKN1A (p21) gains 2 peaks; anti-apoptotic BCL2 and MCL1 each gain 1 peak. The gene with the most gained RUNX1 peaks is SMAD7 (7 peaks), a TGF-beta signaling inhibitor.

Pathways significantly enriched among gained RUNX1 target genes include NF-kB signaling (4.36-fold, p=2.95e-06), MAPK/ERK signaling (3.73-fold, p=6.21e-05), TGF-beta signaling (3.90-fold, p=2.30e-04), MYC network (3.38-fold, p=8.54e-04), and apoptosis regulation (2.76-fold, p=1.47e-03).

These findings support a model where AI-10-49 disrupts CBFbeta-SMMHC, releasing RUNX1 to bind its normal genomic targets — predominantly at active enhancers — where it modulates MYC, cell cycle, and apoptotic gene expression programs to exert its therapeutic effect in inv(16) AML.

RUNX1 chromatin occupancy **massively increases** upon CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition with AI-10-49:

- **6.9× more binding sites** (1,329→9,169 peaks), with **7,950 new sites** gained
- **2.7× stronger signal** at pre-existing sites (93.3% of shared peaks increase)
- **90% of gained sites** overlap H3K27ac-marked active chromatin
- Key gained target genes include **MYC** (at its upstream enhancer), **CCND2**, **CDKN1A/p21**, **BCL2**, **MCL1**, and **SMAD7** (the top gained gene with 7 peaks)
- Significantly enriched pathways: NF-κB (4.36×, p=3e-06), MAPK/ERK (3.73×), TGFβ (3.90×), MYC network (3.38×)

This supports a model where CBFβ-SMMHC sequesters RUNX1 from chromatin; AI-10-49 releases it to bind active enhancers regulating MYC, cell cycle, and apoptosis programs.
